researchScope: Spanish-language Latin America public-health access; Colombia medicine-delivery backlog and existing oversight
intend: Complete one genuinely source-reviewed due Scout cell; persist a public-safe receipt; do not claim a novel defect, outreach, beneficiary outcome, or autonomous specialist execution.

sources.finding: Colombia reports 273,000 patients with some medicine delivery by Oct 5, 39.2% of originally pending medication units delivered, and 168,422 procedures reported resolved. Ministry explicitly states unit-delivery percentages are NOT completed treatment percentages; it is validating procedures and running weekly EPS follow-up through Dec 31.

Earlier official baseline: 177,048 patients and 31.2% pending medicine units dispensed as of Oct 2. Separates patients from units and identifies formal multi-agency control table with patient representatives.
Ombudsman's earlier Nueva EPS oversight documents medicine-delivery failures and discrepancies between administrative indicators and patient experience; does not establish the current October state.
PAHO documents broader regional HIV treatment-access gaps and existing regional alliance; not a new defect requiring Humanity Loop intervention.

findings.verified: Official Colombia Oct 15 release shows progress and outstanding medication units; both government and Ombudsman already acknowledge and monitor patient-level access gaps.
findings.not_verified: No independent October patient-level treatment-completion sample, current Nueva EPS failure rate, or specific newly unreported error was established.
findings.existingSolutions: Ministry weekly EPS monitoring and cross-agency technical control table with patient representation; Ombudsman oversight; PAHO access initiatives.
findings.noveltyAssessment: Low: pre-existing documented access problem with responsible institutions already active; no specific new unaddressed intervention or data defect independently verified.
findings.uncertainty: Ministry figures are administrative, not proof that patients completed treatments. Ombudsman March findings cannot be assumed current in October.
TIPPO: Potential issue: patient experience versus administrative metrics
findings.horizons: H1 current backlog response; H2 possible improved patient-verified accountability; H3 no supported extrapolation

futuresTriangle.push: High medication backlog and ongoing oversight
futuresTriangle.pull: Complete timely treatment and verified patient outcomes

findings.crossImpacts: Partial dispensing may improve administrative progress while failing to restore treatment continuity; transparent denominators mitigate misinterpretation.
findings.falsificationCriteria: A new official data release, independently corroborated patient report, or specific unaddressed access/translation defect demonstrates a tractable new gap; otherwise no additional Humanity Loop case.
findings.decision: NO SIGNAL: no new case, contact, or public accusation; re-evaluate only if an independently verified new gap emerges.
